source.title: Orthogonal Gradient Constraints Shape Noisy-Label Memorization Dynamics

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. No obvious garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own noisy-label experiments. They refine the scope of memorization results by showing that OrthoGrad changes fitting trajectories in some settings but does not prevent eventual noisy-label memorization in the CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label fitting and learning patterns before noisy labels, but those cited results are not this study’s results. Its own experiments use partially corrupted labels, not completely random labels. Figure 2’s weight-norm and gradient-weight-cosine diagnostics describe the OrthoGrad mechanism; they do not measure a claim version directly.
record.test_reason: The study measures noisy-label fitting directly and identifies optimizer-dependent limits to perfect training fit. Its CIFAR-10 trajectories also bear qualitatively on the transition from learning clean labels to memorizing corrupted labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: OrthoGrad reduces corrupted-label fitting and improves test accuracy in some small-data MNIST settings, especially CNNs, but its effects depend on the regime and it does not prevent eventual CIFAR-10 noisy-label memorization.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses partially corrupted labels and modifies Adam updates by projecting weight gradients orthogonally to current weights. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiments. The paper states that architecture, loss, dataset, learning rate, and Adam hyperparameters remain unchanged for the intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by data regime and architecture: it is clearest for small-data MNIST CNNs and weaker or mixed in larger-data MNIST and CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: OrthoGrad improves MNIST test accuracy from 64.0% to 67.7% for the MLP and from 52.2% to 69.0% for the CNN at fixed 30% noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal gradient projection can improve generalization in small-data noisy-label settings.

record.peer_reviewed: HiLD 2026: 4th Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: The experiments focus on small-data MNIST and one CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 extension. The CIFAR-10 trajectory results are described qualitatively, and the text does not give numeric corrupted-label accuracy values. The study does not sweep corruption from none to all.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were omitted. The paper also reports that OrthoGrad lowers corrupted-label accuracy, especially for the small CNN, but gives no numeric value separate from the reported training accuracy; this qualitative statement is summarized in R6’s note rather than added as a duplicate row.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error and chance test performance under the original training recipe.
Relative convergence times for true and random labels, and slowing across corruption fractions.
A corruption sweep from none to all, steadily worsening test performance toward chance, and numerical confirmation of perfect training fit in CIFAR-10.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation and generalization after removing these regularizers. OrthoGrad is a different intervention.
Direct identification of shared-pattern learning, quantitative timing of clean versus noisy-label acquisition, and completely random-label trajectories.

missing.what: A qualitative baseline CIFAR-10 trajectory row: corrupted-label accuracy increases over training while accuracy against original clean labels collapses. Eventual memorization alone does not capture this temporal comparison.
missing.locator: Results, CIFAR-10 extension, paragraph describing the baseline memorization pattern

record.verdict_notes: The V6 evidence is qualitative and weaker than a direct measurement of when shared patterns and individual noisy labels are first learned. Reduced fitting after 400 epochs does not establish permanent prevention of memorization. No figure values beyond those stated in the supplied text are available.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment uses completely random labels or tests zero or near-zero training error and chance test error under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
The study does not compare time to convergence for true versus random labels or measure convergence time across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

The study tests selected corruption settings (30% on MNIST and 20% on CIFAR-10), not a sweep from none to all corruption. It does not establish steadily rising test error toward chance across that sweep.
The study does not test dropout, data augmentation, or whether removing regularization alone harms generalization on true labels.
The study does not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels; this sequencing is cited from prior work.
